scope: Primary-source visual benchmark, not production defect audit. Authoring and rendering remain through json2pptx. No consultant artwork or substantive source text copied into generated decks.
copyright_handling: Source PDFs and page images are private gitignored research evidence; do not commit or distribute as project fixtures. Commit only original illustrative fixture data/rubric if parent chooses.

sources.title: True-Luxury Global Consumer Insights, 11th Edition

pages.observation: One claim leads a time-aligned trend with era shading; signed values and dates appear beside marks. Footnotes are pale and small.
Repeated numbered groups pair dates, values and percentage-point changes. Newspaper images are supporting context; illustrative benchmarks must use original paraphrased evidence.
Segment geometry, multi-year table and interpretation share row relationships. Dense labels compete for attention; treat this as read-ahead, not live density guidance.
Two equal trend panels share year positions and a minus60 to60 percent domain; each has nearby correlation and interpretation. Matching measure colors carry between panels.
Ordinal impact/frequency axes position issues; matching numbers link the diagram to a ranked sidebar. Several labels crowd the plotted region.
Aligned rows pair interview evidence with percentages and implications. This is dense; a live benchmark should use one or two rows.
A central stakeholder relates to four numbered action groups. Connectors explain association; they do not represent time or measured causal effects.

sources.title: Global Private Equity Report2025

pages.observation: Three stacked panels retain quartile order and two-period color meaning; difference brackets state units. Measures differ, so identical vertical domains would be inappropriate.
Stacked regional value bars, a separately labeled count line, aligned deal-size row and change table form one exhibit. Notes qualify exclusions and measurement basis.
Two related trend charts mark forecast intervals with background shading and a label. Sources and scenario vintage appear below; axes differ because measures differ.

sources.title: 29th Global CEO Survey: Leading through uncertainty in the age of AI

sources.classification: Read-ahead report. Standalone exhibits can inspire slides; surrounding prose and research questions require shortening or notes.

pages.observation: A three-by-three outcome grid has direction labels and highlighted subsets connected to interpretations. Callouts identify specific cells rather than floating as decorative cards.
Matched categories and color progression link two outcomes, each with its own explicitly labeled axis. Model adjustments and sample sizes constrain the interpretation.
Two compact paired comparisons use identical category meaning. Research notes define groups and adjustments; whitespace separates exhibit from subsequent narrative.

sources.title: Loose dogs in Dallas: Strategic Recommendations to Improve Public Safety and Animal Welfare
sources.author: Boston Consulting Group; published by City of Dallas

pages.observation: Theme groups highlight selected facts inline, but thirteen bullets create a dense read-ahead page. Use grouped conclusions; do not copy its live density.
Two distinct measures use separate unit labels, focal-city highlighting and benchmark reference lines. An interpretation box explains plausible drivers; long rotated labels reduce live readability.
Impact and effort positions create five action clusters with numbered sequencing. Unequal blocks express categories; long initiative lists make it read-ahead.
Three connected stages associate action groups with ownership, trial execution and measurement. Direction and column alignment establish order.
Rows retain option identities across three criterion columns; ticks and crosses pair with explanations. This is qualitative evidence, not an unexplained numerical score.

guidance_sources.author: Michael Alley, Pennsylvania State University
guidance_sources.derived_principle: Build presentation messages as sentence headlines and support them with visual evidence; secondary detail can go in notes.
guidance_sources.scope: Technical presentation guidance supporting headline/evidence principle, not a universal ban on all bullets.

guidance_sources.author: EU data.europa.eu Data Visualisation Guide
guidance_sources.derived_principle: Faceted comparisons of the same variables need shared scales to aid value comparison.
guidance_sources.scope: Does not require common domains across different metrics.

audience_modes.present: Primary evidence readable as a projected slide at consistent viewport; notes can carry secondary methodology. Shorter content and fewer evidence groups are appropriate.
audience_modes.read-ahead: The artifact is designed for individual reading; sources, definitions and dense supporting tables can remain, with intentional hierarchy and legibility. Portrait reports are not literal live-layout targets.

observable_rubric.name: Evidence supports the headline
observable_rubric.check: Recalculate any stated totals, shares, deltas and relationships; ensure the displayed facts support the claim. Titles can be concise statements; title/section pages are exempt.

observable_rubric.name: Relationships and comparisons
observable_rubric.check: Choose encoding that expresses the task; match domains and plot geometry when comparing the same measure across panels. Distinct outcomes can use separate axes when units and measure names are clear.
observable_rubric.critical_failure: Misleading magnitude, stacking, baseline or unit interpretation.

observable_rubric.name: Reading order and hierarchy
observable_rubric.check: Identify headline, dominant evidence, interpretation and action at full-slide view. Titles must not collide with branded chrome. Similar regions align, while the focal exhibit gets the most area.
observable_rubric.critical_failure: Essential evidence obscured or out of frame.

observable_rubric.name: Labels and explanatory links
observable_rubric.check: Keep categories, series identities, units, bases and callouts near their marks. A label must remain visibly tied to the correct object after layout/crop changes.
observable_rubric.critical_failure: Labels point to wrong values or objects.

observable_rubric.name: Legibility and preservation
observable_rubric.check: Render every final page. At a consistent presentation viewport, primary labels and evidence must be readable without zoom. Inspect note/table detail at read-ahead scale; honor repository template and typography roles. Prefer rearrangement or explicit continuation before losing content.
observable_rubric.critical_failure: Missing content, accidental clipping, overlap or unreadable essential value.

observable_rubric.name: Notes and evidence status
observable_rubric.check: Show measurement basis, unit, period and source or synthetic label; forecast/planning status must be distinguishable from actual observations. Long methodological detail belongs in notes/appendix without dropping its essential qualification.
observable_rubric.critical_failure: Forecast or illustrative content presented as measured actuals.

observable_rubric.name: Template portability
observable_rubric.check: Review all10 local templates including gitignored p-style. Respect theme fonts, colors, reserved chrome, contrast and content zones; retain semantic equality while changing layout.
observable_rubric.critical_failure: Template-specific clipping, wrong theme, invisible essential evidence or content loss.

observable_rubric.name: Decision and narrative coherence
observable_rubric.check: For decision decks, distinguish diagnosis, options, recommendation and execution. Owners, dates and gates must agree across slides; deck rhythm should reflect different evidence structures.
observable_rubric.critical_failure: Conflicting decisions, owners, dates or gate conditions.

scoring: Record each applicable rubric item as pass, needs_improvement or fail, with screenshot/shape evidence. No aggregate percentage substitutes for critical failures. Record subjective aesthetic preferences separately from defects.

latest_consultant_comparison: Recent BCG2025 and PwC2026 exhibits use fact statements, repeated identities, coordinated comparison regions and explicit qualifications. Bain2025 adds rigorous supporting tables and forecast labels. These qualities are relationship/semantics requirements rather than demand for decorative consulting artwork. The actual Dallas client deck confirms decision and prioritization structures but also shows why published consultant density is not an unquestioned live-slide standard.
visual_inspection_protocol: Render every final slide for each of10 local templates, including p-style.
Inspect at one consistent full-slide viewport for headline and primary evidence, then detail zoom for notes and fit.
Compare composition intent against the relevant source exhibit, preserving theme identity and original illustrative data.
Check every value/delta, scale, forecast marker, note, source and linked label before cosmetic scoring.
Use shape/frame analysis to substantiate suspected clipping or overflow; a screenshot alone can be ambiguous.
Retain before/after repro images and specification when filing an atomic defect; distinguish input repair from renderer failure.
